title: Inside the FBI's two-tiered approach of attack: Aggressive on Trump, protective on Biden - Whatfinger News Quick Hits
text:
The FBI led multiple operations prior to the 2020 election that helped politically and financially damage President Donald Trump and, at the same time, protect then-presidential candidate Joe Biden from law enforcement.Two operations – Crossfire Hurricane and Oxferd Comma – served to undermine Trump and paint him as a Russian operative by zealously investigating unsubstantiated allegations pushed by Democrats. Running in tandem with those investigations was Round River, which was designed to fight “malign foreign influence” by ignoring actual evidence of corruption and crimes involving the Biden family and paint any Republican who questioned that family as a conspiracy theorist or Russian asset.
Crossfire Hurricane targeted Trump over Democrat paid-for allegations
Crossfire Hurricane involved the abuse of surveillance rules during the Obama administration allowing the FBI and other intelligence agencies to target the Trump campaign under the guise of fighting foreign influence. Based on unsubstantiated allegations pushed by the Clinton campaign, the investigation involved undercover informants infiltrating the Trump campaign to try and lure out incriminating evidence – which never came. An Inspector General report from the Department of Justice released in 2019 admitted some of that surveillance was “unlawful.”
The Inspector General report found that the FBI altered evidence against Trump campaign adviser Carter Page in order to investigate him, leading to FBI attorney Kevin Clinesmith pleading guilty in 2020 to falsifying an email for the purposes of obtaining a FISA warrant.
That warrant authorized spying on Page and his interactions with the Trump campaign. Page had worked with the CIA dealing with Russians in the early days of the Obama administration, but Clinesmith altered an email to make it appear as though Page had never worked with the agency.
Declassified records released by the FBI and obtained by Just the News show Stefan Halper, an informant who also worked as a Pentagon researcher, was directed to meet with Page at a Virginia farm in October 2016, to try to elicit information about the campaign’s possible ties to Russia. Other declassified documents show that Halper was paid nearly $1.2 million by the FBI over three decades.
The FBI also sent an undercover operative to meet with Trump campaign aide George Papadopoulos while posing as a research assistant named Azra Turk, according to reporting from The New York Times in 2019. The investigators attempted to get Papadopoulos to falsely admit the Trump campaign was working with Russia. Halper was also asked by the FBI to speak with Papadopoulos about alleged Russia collusion, records show.
Special Counsel: “No criminal conspiracy between Vladimir Putin’s Russia and the Trump campaign.”
Special Counsel Robert Mueller’s massive investigation into Russia collusion determined there was no criminal conspiracy between Vladimir Putin’s Russia and the Trump campaign.
A second Special Counsel, John Durham, went even further, concluding during the Biden administration that the Obama-era FBI and DOJ had no basis to open an investigation of Trump-Russia collusion.
“Neither U.S. law enforcement nor the Intelligence Community appears to have possessed any actual evidence of collusion in their holdings at the commencement of the Crossfire Hurricane investigation,” Durham wrote in a 300-plus page report sent to Congress in spring 2023.
Declassified documents pertaining to Crossfire Hurricane released in April 2025 revealed that the FBI had doubts about the authenticity of the allegations against Trump, but pursued the president anyway.
Oxferd Comma
Oxferd Comma began eight days after Trump fired then-FBI Director James Comey in 2017. The FBI knew that the firing had nothing to do with Russia, but investigated the sitting president anyway.
“The FBI is opening a full investigation based on an articulable factual basis that reasonably indicates that President Donald J. Trump may be or has been, wittingly or unwittingly, involved in activities for or on behalf of the Government of the Russian Federation which may constitute violations of federal criminal law or threats to the national security of the United States,” reads the electronic communication, approved by then-FBI General Counsel James Baker and then-Assistant Director for Counterintelligence William Priestap.
“The goal of the investigation is to determine if President Trump is or was directed by, controlled by, and/or coordinated activities with, the Russian Federation in a manner constituting a threat to the national security of the United States and/or a violation of federal criminal statutes,” the memo added. “In addition, this investigation will also seek to determine whether President Trump and others yet to be named obstructed and/or conspiracy to obstruct any associated FBI investigation.”
The memo went on to make clear the investigation was tied to Crossfire Hurricane, even though in both instances, the FBI knew or had doubts about the authenticity of the allegations against Trump.
Round River
In contrast to the two above investigations into Trump, the Round River operation sought to discredit anyone suggesting corruption amongst members of the Biden family – and actively suppressed information that confirmed that corruption.
As Just the News reported Wednesday, the FBI had 14 informants with information on Biden family corruption but worked to portray Biden and other Democrats as victims of Russian disinformation from conservative news sites, painting every story as “Russian disinformation.” Prominent Republicans were labeled as “conduits” of Russian disinformation.
Confidential Human Sources (CHS) reported concerns about the Biden family and its ties to Ukraine beginning in 2015, but labeled former Attorney General Bill Barr’s investigation into that corruption as a conspiracy theory and Barr himself as a conspiracy theorist or Russian asset.
Other agencies helped Biden and undermined Trump, media played same game
In addition to the FBI and IRS, others helped Biden in 2020 and undermined Trump, including 51 former intelligence officials who signed a now infamous letter claiming a bombshell report from The New York Post about the contents of Hunter Biden’s laptop was Russian disinformation. The officials knew this was not true, but coordinated with the Biden campaign and then-Secretary of State Antony Blinken to release the letter prior to Biden’s debate with Trump, so Biden could dismiss a major Trump talking point. When Trump came back into office in 2025, he revoked the security clearances of the former intelligence officials who signed the letter.
The FBI under Biden also pressured social media sites to censor the laptop story, with former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey later admitting that censoring the story was wrong. Facebook executives also suppressed the story to gain favor with the Biden administration, the House Judiciary Committee’s subcommittee on the weaponization of government found in 2024.
